note: Unselected T2D; exenatide (2005) founded the class and liraglutide, dulaglutide and semaglutide followed; tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist and is not scored here.
label: Type 2 diabetes (GLP-1)

engagement.note: GLP-1(7-37) raised insulin release 3-10-fold in the perfused rat pancreas only with glucose present; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: GLP-1 insulinotropic in perfused rat pancreas
engagement.quote: In the presence of 6.6 mM glucose, GLP-I(7-37) is a potent stimulator of insulin secretion at concentrations as low as 5 X 10(-11) M (3- to 10-fold increases over basal).

engagement.note: IV GLP-1 raised insulin, cut glucagon and normalised fasting glucose in 10 T2D patients; insulin fell back once glucose normalised, as the rat pancreas predicted.
engagement.short: Glucose-dependent insulinotropism held in T2D patients
engagement.quote: When normal fasting plasma glucose concentrations were reached insulin returned towards basal levels and plasma glucose concentrations remained stable despite the ongoing infusion of GLP-1 (7-36 amide).
engagement.reason: Insulin, glucagon, glucose moved as predicted
engagement.judgement: Native GLP-1 infused as a pharmacological agonist is taken as the class prototype (the human physiology predates the drugs); the first marketed analog reproduced the same glucose-dependent insulin/glucagon pattern in T2D patients (Kolterman 2003, doi:10.1210/jc.2002-021545). Abstract-level, paywalled; the juxtaposition with Mojsov 1987 is the drafter's, not the source's. The model was dosed with GLP-1(7-37), patients with GLP-1(7-36)amide: both native forms.

dose.model: db/db mice, ZDF rats, diabetic rhesus monkeys
dose.note: Exendin-4 ED50 for glucose lowering was 0.059 ug/kg in db/db mice and 0.25 ug/kg in diabetic rhesus monkeys; no patient dose yet.
dose.quote: Exendin-4 dose-dependently accelerated glucose lowering in diabetic rhesus monkeys by up to 37% with an ED50 of 0.25 microg/kg +/-0.09 log.

dose.model: db/db mice, ZDF rats, diabetic rhesus monkeys
dose.note: 0.05-0.2 ug/kg exenatide lowered fasting and postprandial glucose in T2D patients; the fixed 5-10 ug clinical dose (~0.05-0.1 ug/kg) sits inside the animal ED50 range.
dose.short: Patient dose 0.1 ug/kg matched animal ED50
dose.quote: In study B, 13 subjects receiving a single dose of study medication (0.05, 0.1, or 0.2 micro g/kg AC2993 or placebo) following an overnight fast had reduced fasting plasma glucose concentrations during the subsequent 8-h period.
dose.reason: Clinical ug/kg dose inside animal ED50 range
dose.judgement: Called same by juxtaposing the Young 1999 ED50s (0.059 ug/kg db/db mouse, 0.25 ug/kg rhesus) with the 0.05-0.2 ug/kg doses that lowered glucose in patients; Kolterman 2003 is an Amylin paper but does not tabulate the animal numbers alongside. Within 2x of the monkey ED50. Abstract-level, paywalled. The 2005 FDA pharmacology review could not be opened (Drugs@FDA index 404), so model_filed is left null. A stricter reading (no source states the comparison) would leave this cell untested.

efficacy.model: db/db mice, ZDF rats, diabetic rhesus monkeys
efficacy.note: Twice-daily exendin-4 for 5-6 weeks lowered HbA1c and body weight in diabetic fatty Zucker rats; rodent weight-loss ED50 1.0 ug/kg.
efficacy.short: Exendin-4 lowered HbA1c and weight in ZDF rats
efficacy.quote: In conclusion, acute and chronic administration of exendin-4 has demonstrated an antidiabetic effect in several animal models of type 2 diabetes.

efficacy.model: db/db mice, ZDF rats, diabetic rhesus monkeys
efficacy.note: 30-week exenatide 10 ug b.i.d. cut HbA1c 0.86% and weight 1.6 kg in 377 sulfonylurea-treated T2D patients; direction matched, weight effect far smaller than rodents'.
efficacy.quote: At week 30, HbA(1c) changes from baseline were -0.86 +/- 0.11, -0.46 +/- 0.12, and 0.12 +/- 0.09% (+/-SE) in the 10-microg, 5-microg, and placebo arms, respectively (adjusted P < 0.001).
efficacy.reason: HbA1c and weight fell as rodents predicted
efficacy.judgement: Same, not neg: no GLP-1 agonist that worked in db/db or ZDF later failed on glucose in patients (taspoglutide was withdrawn for tolerability/immunogenicity, not efficacy). Two rodent predictions did not carry: ~15% body-weight loss in rats (Larsen 2001, doi:10.2337/diabetes.50.11.2530) versus ~2% in T2D patients, and the db/db beta-cell mass expansion (Rolin 2002, doi:10.1152/ajpendo.00030.2002) has never been demonstrable in humans; both are magnitude or secondary-endpoint misses, so the primary glucose prediction keeps the cell at same. Juxtaposed by the drafter. Registered as NCT00039026 (first posted 2002-06-10) but no results were ever posted, so registry_date is null.

safety.note: 104-week rat bioassay: benign thyroid C-cell adenomas in female rats at all exenatide doses (5-130x human AUC); mice tumour-free; no patient comparison.
safety.short: Rat C-cell adenomas at all doses
safety.quote: Benign thyroid C-cell adenomas were observed in female rats at all exenatide doses.

safety.note: Rodent C-cells express GLP-1R and proliferate; primate C-cells barely do, 20-month monkey study and 2-year patient calcitonin showed nothing; FDA still boxed the warning.
safety.short: Rodent C-cell tumours not seen in primates
safety.quote: In contrast, humans and/or cynomolgus monkeys had low GLP-1 receptor expression in thyroid C-cells, and GLP-1 receptor agonists did not activate adenylate cyclase or generate calcitonin release in primates.
safety.judgement: Scored contra as a false positive: the rodent bioassay predicted C-cell tumours, patients showed no calcitonin rise at 2 years and later no thyroid-cancer excess (Pasternak 2024 BMJ, HR 0.93, 145,410 users; doi:10.1136/bmj-2023-078225). One dissent: Bezin 2023 French case-control (HR 1.58 all thyroid cancer, 1.78 MTC; doi:10.2337/dc22-1148). The alternative reading is untested (MTC too rare and slow to compare), which is what the January 2010 Victoza boxed warning says: human relevance 'could not be ruled out by clinical or nonclinical studies' (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2010/022341lbl.pdf). Sponsor-authored source; the 2-year patient calcitonin data are the LEAD-3 extension (NCT00294723, results first posted 2010-03-12).

safety.note: Pancreatitis: tox in 3 species silent at 60x human exposure; 2010 label counted 7 vs 1 trial cases; FDA/EMA 2014 found no causal link.
safety.short: Pancreatitis: animals silent, human signal unproven
safety.quote: In conclusion, liraglutide did not induce pancreatitis in mice, rats, or monkeys when dosed for up to 2 years and at exposure levels up to 60 times higher than in humans.
safety.judgement: Status unchanged (contra carries from the C-cell story); entry added because the pancreatitis comparison was requested. Patient side: Victoza 2010 label 5.2 reports 7 vs 1 pancreatitis cases (2.2 vs 0.6 per 1000 patient-years) in the LEAD programme; the FDA/EMA joint assessment (Egan 2014, doi:10.1056/NEJMp1314078; paywalled, could not be quoted) concluded the data do not support a causal association, so the animal silence has not been contradicted but the question is open. Sponsor-authored source; registry_date is LEAD-3 as the representative LEAD trial.
